metadata.title: MatriSync India-focused medication reference catalogue
metadata.frequency_basis: Practical catalogue-building priority; not measured prescribing prevalence
metadata.scope: Women of reproductive age; pregnancy, postpartum and exposure recognition
metadata.limitations:
This is an India-focused, prioritised catalogue of 162 medicines, combinations and vaccine types relevant to women of reproductive age, with particular attention to pregnancy and the postpartum period. It is a broad starting formulary, not an exhaustive inventory of all Indian products or a measured national prescribing-frequency ranking.

The first 69 entries cover everyday supplements, symptom medicines and common infection treatments. They are followed by 26 obstetric medicines, 38 entries for long-term conditions/special infections/immunisation, 22 exposure-alert entries and 7 other women-health entries. Priority means catalogue-building order, not a recommendation to prescribe. Add exposure alerts to the first checker release even though they appear later in the reading order.

Listing does not mean that a medicine is appropriate for every pregnant patient. Some entries are deliberately included because exposure requires review. Decisions depend on diagnosis, gestational age, dose, duration, route, allergies, organ function and other medicines. Patients should not start, stop or switch long-term medicines from this catalogue alone.

Generic ingredients are used instead of brands. The selection is relevant to Indian practice, but current Indian brand licences, strengths, formulations, stock and local prescribing frequency have not been verified product by product. NLEM inclusion is not claimed for every entry, and NLEM itself is not a pregnancy-safety list. International pregnancy references supplement Indian programme guidance; their schedules or marketing authorisations do not automatically apply in India.

Every record contains a professional and a plain-English class, mechanism and use description. Routes identify possible formulations, not permission to use every route for every listed indication. Pregnancy notes highlight important issues but are not full monographs. Dose regimens, full contraindication lists, lactation assessments and a complete interaction matrix are outside this catalogue. A postpartum use is not automatically a pregnancy or breastfeeding endorsement.

Evidence status: source-informed draft for clinical review, prepared 15 October 2026. Reference links support the relevant class, use or pregnancy context; they are not proof of all details in a row. Mechanisms are concise pharmacology summaries and need product-specific monograph verification before clinical release. No clinician approval or database licensing review is implied. The JSON deliberately marks every record as not released for clinical decision support.

priorities.A: Everyday catalogue: supplements, symptom medicines and common infections; not all are first-line or routine pregnancy treatment.
priorities.B: Pregnancy-specific indications, complications, labour and postpartum care.
priorities.C: Long-term conditions, specialist infections and immunisation.
priorities.D: Exposure recognition and pregnancy alerts; import alerts from day one, not after the other tiers.
priorities.E: Other women-health medicines used before conception or after birth; not routine pregnancy maintenance.

medicines.name: Folic acid
medicines.section: 01 Everyday: nutrients and supplements

professional.mechanism: Converted to reduced folates for one-carbon transfer, nucleotide synthesis and erythropoiesis.
professional.uses: Neural-tube-defect prevention; folate-deficiency anaemia.

plain_language.mechanism: Helps cells make DNA and healthy red blood cells.
plain_language.uses: Supports early brain and spinal development and treats low folate.

medicines.pregnancy_context: Important before conception and in early pregnancy; also in antenatal IFA. Higher-risk dosing requires a clinician. Do not treat unexplained anaemia without assessing B12.

implementation_notes:
## What this catalogue gives MatriSync

An ingredient-oriented reference layer with stable draft IDs, reading priority, category, routes, two explanation levels, pregnancy-context notes and a source registry. It can support a prototype medicine search and clinician review workflow. It is not an executable interaction engine, a prescribing protocol or a validated patient-facing clinical dataset.

## Required next database layers

| Layer | Minimum information |
|---|---|
| Ingredient identity | Canonical ingredient ID, aliases, salt/active-moiety relationship, verified terminology code and separate combination ingredients. Do not invent ATC/RxNorm codes. |
| Indian product mapping | Brand, manufacturer, active ingredients, strength, units, release type, formulation, route, pack and current licence/formulary verification. Different products with similar brand names can differ. |
| Patient context | Pregnancy status and gestational age in weeks/days, postpartum interval, breastfeeding, allergies, indication, renal/liver function, relevant laboratory results and actual exposure dates. |
| Interaction rules | Ingredient pair, mechanism, evidence, clinical importance, dose/route/timing conditions, onset, action, monitoring and authoritative source/version. |
| Pregnancy rules | Ingredient plus indication, dose, route, gestational window, evidence and action. Keep fetal risk separate from drug-drug interactions. |
| Other checks | Duplicate ingredients/classes, allergy, disease contraindications, renal/hepatic adjustment, food/herbal interactions and IV compatibility as separate rule types. |
| Governance | Clinical reviewer and approval date, source permissions/licence, rule version, review due date, audit history and withdrawal/replacement process. |

Do not derive an interaction simply because two medicines have similar mechanisms. Do not inherit a class warning across every drug, route, dose or gestational stage without verifying applicability. Combination decomposition in this JSON covers only five explicit drug combinations; vaccines, ORS, salt forms, supplements and Indian brand combinations need product-level modelling.

## High-value examples for the rule-review queue

These are educational examples, not a comprehensive set of implemented or validated rules.

| Situation | Type of check | Review message | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oral iron with calcium | Absorption interaction | Do not schedule together by default; apply the selected product/programme timing guidance. | CAL |
| Levothyroxine with iron/calcium | Absorption interaction | Separate administration by at least four hours and assess thyroid control. | LT4, THYROID |
| Dolutegravir with iron/calcium | Conditional absorption interaction | Fasting: dolutegravir two hours before or six hours after. Iron/calcium can be taken together with dolutegravir with food under label guidance. This food exception must not be applied automatically to magnesium/aluminium antacids. | DTG |
| Domperidone with erythromycin or another QT/CYP3A4 risk drug | Drug-drug cardiac interaction | Check label contraindications and seek an alternative where required; do not merely display a mild generic caution. | DOM |
| Warfarin with miconazole, including oral gel | Drug-drug interaction | Potentially severe anticoagulant potentiation; pharmacist/prescriber review and product-specific management are required. | MICO |
| Methylergometrine with significant CYP3A4 inhibitors | Drug-drug interaction | Avoid combinations prohibited by the label because of vasospasm/toxicity risk. | METHYL |
| NSAID exposure at or after 20 weeks | Drug-pregnancy check | Review fetal kidney/amniotic-fluid risk and later ductal risk; prescribed low-dose aspirin is a distinct indication-specific case. | NSAID |
| Methylergometrine in pre-eclampsia; carboprost in asthma | Drug-disease check | These are maternal contraindication/precaution checks, not ordinary drug-pair interactions. | METHYL, CARBO |
| Nitrofurantoin selected for suspected kidney infection | Drug-indication check | Lower-urinary-tract activity does not make it adequate for pyelonephritis. | UTI |
| Two brand products containing paracetamol | Duplicate-ingredient check | Add all paracetamol exposure before evaluating the total regimen. | PARA |

The intended UI outcome for an unreviewed ingredient or pair is “Not yet checked: clinical review needed”, not “No interaction” or “Safe in pregnancy”. Even a reviewed pair with no known interaction does not establish pregnancy suitability. For offline operation, distribute a versioned, clinically approved reference bundle; show its review date and preserve previous versions for audit. Synchronise updates when connectivity returns.

## Coverage boundaries

This v0.1 catalogue does not attempt to list every Indian brand, strength, fixed-dose combination, anaesthetic, ICU/sepsis medicine, oncology agent, biologic, Ayurvedic/herbal preparation, nutraceutical mixture or lactation-specific treatment. Product labels and current local formularies are required before asserting availability. Broader coverage should be driven by actual de-identified facility prescriptions and medication histories, with pharmacist/OBG review. Do not interpret omission as absence of risk.

Do not label every nutrient as universally needed. Do not treat every progestogen as the same medicine. Do not treat an oral antifungal as equivalent to a vaginal preparation. Do not apply retired FDA A/B/C/D/X categories as a single universal safety score.
